what_its_for: Aflibercept-ayyh is used to treat certain eye conditions that can cause vision loss. These include wet age-related macular degeneration (wet AMD), diabetic macular edema (DME), and macular edema following retinal vein occlusion (RVO). It works by blocking a protein called VEGF that causes abnormal blood vessels to grow and leak in your eye.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection directly into your eye (called an intravitreal injection) by your eye doctor. You will not give this injection yourself. Your doctor will numb your eye before the injection so you feel little or no pain. The procedure takes only a few minutes and is done in your doctor's office or clinic. Your eye will be cleaned carefully before the injection to prevent infection.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose and how often you need injections based on your eye condition. A typical schedule may start with one injection every month for the first few months, and then less frequently over time. Always follow your doctor's specific schedule. Do not miss any scheduled appointments, as staying on schedule is important for protecting your vision.
missed_dose: If you miss or need to reschedule an injection appointment, call your eye doctor as soon as possible to set up a new appointment. Do not wait too long between doses, as this could allow your eye condition to get worse. Your doctor will advise you on the best time to reschedule.
storage: Aflibercept-ayyh is stored and handled by your doctor or healthcare provider. You will not need to store this medicine at home. Your doctor's office keeps it refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C) and protects it from light. Do not freeze the medication.
what_to_avoid: After your eye injection, avoid rubbing or touching your eye, as this can cause infection or injury. Do not swim or use hot tubs for at least 24 to 48 hours after the injection. Avoid dusty or smoky environments right after treatment. Tell your doctor about all other medications, eye drops, or supplements you are taking, as some may not be safe to use together.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden changes in vision, increased eye pain or redness, sensitivity to light, floaters (dots or lines floating in your vision), or a feeling that something is in your eye after the injection. These could be signs of a serious eye infection (endophthalmitis) or other complications. Also tell your doctor if you have signs of a stroke or heart attack such as chest pain, sudden weakness, numbness, or trouble speaking.
when_it_works: You may not notice results right away. Some patients begin to see improvement in their vision within a few weeks to months after starting treatment. However, the main goal of this medicine is often to stop your vision from getting worse. It may take several injections before you notice a benefit. Be patient and keep all of your scheduled appointments.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before receiving this medicine. It is not known if aflibercept-ayyh is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 months after the last injection. This medicine has not been studied in children. Older adults can receive this medicine and do not typically need a dose adjustment, but your doctor will monitor you carefully.
